description: I am a student interested in research, international issues, technology, and creative problem-solving. I enjoy connecting research with real-world challenges.
summary:
ORBIVUE is a satellite-based risk intelligence concept designed for maritime areas. It uses observations from the NASA–ISRO NISAR mission along with geospatial data to assess environmental risks that affect coastal zones and maritime activities.
Our early research has helped shape a proposed workflow. This workflow is meant to turn satellite observations into useful information. The information is designed to be relevant to decision-making. Potential users include port operators, coastal infrastructure developers and other relevant institutions.
ORBIVUE fills the gap, between Earth observation data and practical decision-making. It connects satellite monitoring with information needs. The project aims to support risk assessment, planning and resilience efforts. This is important because coastal communities and maritime infrastructure are facing increasing pressures. They need information to understand these risks and respond effectively.
details:
ORBIVUE is a satellite-based Coastal and Maritime Risk Intelligence concept. It uses observations from the NASA–ISRO NISAR mission together with complementary geospatial datasets to assess environmental risks affecting coastal areas and maritime activities.
The proposed workflow consists of four stages: collecting satellite and geospatial data, integrating relevant datasets, examining environmental indicators linked to risk, and translating analytical findings into accessible outputs such as geospatial maps, location-based assessment summaries, and reports.

ORBIVUE wants to make complicated Earth observation data easy to understand and useful for port operators people who build infrastructure, insurance companies, risk assessors and public agencies. By giving a view of environmental conditions and risks ORBIVUE helps people plan better manage infrastructure and strengthen coastal resilience.

The creative part of ORBIVUE is linking satellite radar data with real risk assessment needs. Of showing satellite images as separate facts ORBIVUE mixes many geospatial sources and shows the results in ways that users can read and use.

Now ORBIVUE is only doing research building the idea and sketching early designs. The research has looked at NISARs Earth observation power, other datasets, likely users and possible assessment rules. ORBIVUE has not yet made a working platform. Tested any analytical model. The next actions are to set assessment rules check how suitable the data are, collect user needs and build a demo.

Far ORBIVUE has done desk research looked at technology and made a conceptual design. No working prototype has been. ORBIVUE has not used any programming languages or hardware yet. The research has used NISAR mission documents, Earth observation material and other geospatial data. These will guide ORBIVUEs technical work.

Important things ORBIVUE thinks about are how available and reliable the data are, how well satellite observations fit environmental conditions how accurate and clear the risk signs are, what users need, whether the tech can work and how useful the outputs really are.

ORBIVUE is an independent project concept and is not affiliated with or endorsed by NASA or ISRO.
